These are the lecture notes for the first part of ENGI 1111, Thermodynamics and
Fluid Mechanics I.

**This site is the lecture.** The gaps start covered; in class we uncover them
one at a time. It is also the version that stays up afterwards, so what you saw
on the screen and what you can re-read later are the same page — there is no
second, slightly different set of "completed notes" to reconcile against your
own.

| | What it is | When to use it |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Student copy (PDF)** | the notes with the gaps left blank | print it and bring it — you fill the gaps in as we go |
| **This site** | the same notes, uncovered step by step | in the lecture, and any time afterwards |
| **Completed copy (PDF)** | everything already uncovered | if you would rather have the finished version on paper |

Problems now sit at the end of the chapter they belong to, rather than on a
separate weekly sheet. Each one has space for your own working; on this site the
worked solution is covered until you choose to open it.

- [CH2 — First Law of Thermodynamics](ch02-first-law.qmd)

Chapters 3–6 are still in the old format on Ultra while they are being
converted.

## Supplementary books

- *Thermodynamics* by A. M. Steane (available online)
- *Fundamentals of Thermodynamics*, 7th ed., by C. Borgnakke and R. E. Sonntag
- *Moran's Principles of Engineering Thermodynamics*, 9th ed., by M. J. Moran
- *Engineering Thermodynamics: Work & Heat Transfer*, 4th ed., by Rogers & Mayhew
